output.proposal: HB No. 11018 seeks to establish the Bicol River Basin Management Office (BRBMO), attached to the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), as the central coordinating and implementing body for river basin-related programs, projects and policies in the Bicol River Basin. It aims to promote integrated river basin management through inter-agency coordination and stakeholder participation, given the basin's role in flood control, agriculture, water security and regional development.
output.alignment: As a government organization measure, the review should examine how the functions of the proposed BRBMO under Section 5 (Powers and Functions) fit with those of existing bodies with river basin mandates, including the River Basin Control Office named in Section 7 (Coordination with Existing Agencies (Non-Impairment Clause)), the DENR, the National Irrigation Administration, the Department of Public Works and Highways and the LGUs, as well as earlier issuances creating Bicol River Basin offices and councils, and whether the creation of a new office is consistent with the intent to streamline the Executive branch and reduce overlapping functions under the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231). No direct match with an FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework priority area or the LEDAC Common Legislative Agenda was identified.
legislative_history: HB No. 11018 was filed in the House of Representatives on September 1, 2026 by Representative Alfred Delos Santos during the 20th Congress.
Its current status is Filed; later stages are not reflected in the available information.
No earlier version, counterpart in the Senate, substitute bill or committee report for this measure was identified.

output.salient_features:
HB No. 11018 seeks to establish the Bicol River Basin Management Office (BRBMO) as the coordinating and implementing body for the Bicol River Basin. Its salient features are as follows:
a. Section 2 (Declaration of Policy) provides that the State shall promote integrated river basin management through inter-agency coordination and stakeholder participation and strengthen institutional mechanisms for the Bicol River Basin.
b. Section 3 (Creation of the Bicol River Basin Management Office (BRBMO)) provides that the BRBMO shall serve as the central coordinating and implementing body for river basin-related programs, projects and policies in the basin, and shall be attached to the DENR for policy and program coordination.
c. Section 4 (Coverage) provides that the BRBMO's jurisdiction covers the entire Bicol River Basin, including areas in Camarines Sur, Albay and other adjoining areas as the DENR may determine.
d. Section 5 (Powers and Functions) provides that the BRBMO shall formulate and implement an Integrated River Basin Management Plan, coordinate national agencies, LGUs and stakeholders, monitor and evaluate basin projects, facilitate flood control, watershed, irrigation and water resource initiatives, and promote climate resilience and disaster risk reduction.
e. Section 6 (Organizational Structure) provides that the BRBMO shall be headed by an Executive Director appointed by the President, supported by technical, administrative and support staff as necessary; no salary grade is specified.
f. Section 7 (Coordination with Existing Agencies (Non-Impairment Clause)) provides that the BRBMO shall not diminish the mandates of the DENR, the River Basin Control Office, the National Irrigation Administration, the DPWH and LGUs, and shall operate primarily as a coordinative body.
g. Section 8 (Consultation with Communities, Local People's Organizations, and Civil Society Organizations) provides for regular consultations, representation of communities and organizations in planning bodies, and feedback and grievance mechanisms.
h. Section 9 (Roles of Local Government Units) provides that LGUs in the basin shall participate in planning and implementation and align local plans with the basin plan while retaining their autonomy.
i. Section 10 (Appropriation) provides that the amount needed for implementation shall be included in the annual General Appropriations Act.
j. Section 11 (Implementing Rules and Regulations) provides that the DENR, in coordination with relevant agencies, shall issue the implementing rules within ninety days from effectivity.
output.related_measures_policy: HB No. 11018 may be considered alongside existing issuances on Bicol River Basin institutions, namely PD No. 926 on the organizational structure of the Bicol River Basin Program, EO No. 412 (1973) creating the Bicol River Basin Council, EO No. 359 (2004) creating the Bicol River Basin Project Management Office and EO No. 711 (2008) on the Bicol River Basin water management project, as well as EO No. 510 (2006) creating the River Basin Control Office. It may also be viewed alongside pending 20th Congress measures proposing river basin development authorities for other basins, such as HB No. 3119 (Abra River Basin) and HB No. 1098 (Chico River Basin), for consistency in institutional design. No direct link to the FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework or the LEDAC Common Legislative Agenda was identified. The review should assess whether the functions under Section 5 (Powers and Functions) duplicate those of the River Basin Control Office and existing Bicol River Basin offices, how Section 7 (Coordination with Existing Agencies (Non-Impairment Clause)) and Section 13 (Repealing Clause) affect those issuances, and whether a new office is warranted under the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231).

reviewer_checks: Section 3 refers to 'the created' BRBMO without an express creation clause; confirm the intended wording.
Section 6 does not state the salary grade of the Executive Director or the staffing complement, which are needed to estimate costs.
Confirm whether PD No. 926, EO No. 412 (1973), EO No. 359 (2004) and EO No. 711 (2008) remain in force and how the BRBMO relates to the offices they created.
Clarify which EO No. 359 the bill refers to, since several issuances share that number.
Check the relationship between the BRBMO and the River Basin Control Office, both linked to the DENR.
Section 13 uses a general repealing clause; confirm whether specific issuances should be expressly repealed or amended.
